title: Annotatio IV §.XIV open: Tenth century — Baronius/Bellarmine dark age; yet genuine Supper witnesses
pass_a_gloss: §. XIV. The TENTH AGE has been marked by Baronius in the Annals with coal black enough — called iron for sterility of the good, leaden for the deformity of overflowing evil, obscure finally for want of Writers — and has even earned this indignant exclamation of BELLARMINE: See an unhappy Age, in which no illustrious Writers, no Councils, Pontiffs little solicitous for the republic — understand Ecclesiastical;
pass_b_english: §.XIV: Baronius marks the TENTH age with black coal — iron for sterility of good, leaden for overflowing evil, obscure for want of writers.
Bellarmine’s cry: unhappy age — no illustrious writers, no councils, pontiffs little solicitous for the ecclesiastical republic.
source_text: §. XIV. SECULUM X, à Baronio in Annalibus atrô satis carbone notatum est, ob boni sterilitatem, ferreum, mali exundantis deformitatem, plumbeum, ob inopiam denique Scriptorum, obscurum nuncupatum, BELLARMINI etiam indignabundam hanc exclamationem promeritum: Vide Seculum infelix, in quo nulli Scriptores illustres, nulla Concilia, Pontifices parum solliciti de republica, subintellige Ecclesiastica;
